outcome: circulating maternal placental biomarkers (PlGF, sFlt-1/PlGF ratio)
cohort: The study included 447 pregnancies, comparing 117 women with diabetes mellitus in pregnancy (DIP) and small fetuses (<20th centile for gestational age) to 330 non-diabetic women with similarly small fetuses.
finding: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy (DIP) is associated with increased risks of early-onset FGR, preterm birth, composite severe non-neurological neonatal morbidity, and neonatal hypoglycemia in women with small infants.
mod_finding: DIP was associated with higher rates of emergency cesarean section (43.6% vs. 26.7%).
birth_weight: 2300g (1558-2610g) for DIP cohort vs. 2447g (2050-2690g) for non-diabetic cohort
gest_age: Fetuses defined as <20th centile for gestational age; outcomes included preterm birth <37 weeks and <34 weeks' gestation.
